83.0.0.en: 1- Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.

83.0.1.en: 1- The psalmist speaks here in the voice of God's people who see the plots of the enemies surrounding them. So he says to Him: Though I in my weakness am silent, You do not be silent, but speak, for one word from Your mouth drives all the wicked away from me.

83.0.2.en: 2- The enemies are not only the peoples surrounding God's people, but this psalm is a symbol of the enemies who fight God's people in the New Testament, whether those who live alongside them from among non-Christians or those who are in their midst such as the heretics..

83.1.0.en: 2- For, lo, thine enemies roar: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head. 3- They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy protected ones.

83.1.1.en: Roar: they make loud noises like the sound of waves dashing in a troubled sea. Protected ones: those whom You protect.

83.1.2.en: 1- The enemies of God's people gathered to wrong them; therefore he said "have lifted up the head", for they have one head, who is Satan and evil, and they make loud, unintelligible noises, that is, they have no argument in their agitation against God's people, but it is something that has filled their hearts against the innocent people of God, and we see in these enemies many evils, which are:

83.1.3.en: a- They gathered in great numbers to fight God's people.

83.1.4.en: b- They were proud toward God's people; for they lifted up the head.

83.1.5.en: c- They were malicious, so they devised plots with cunning in secret against God's people.

83.1.6.en: d- They held many consultations and plots in order to inflict great harm on the children of God.

83.1.7.en: 2- The psalmist evokes God's mercies, for he says to Him that these wicked are Your enemies and haters; so that God may arise and defend His people, especially since they were bold and made light of God in wronging His people.

83.2.0.en: 4- They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. 5- For they have consulted together with one heart: they are confederate against thee:

83.2.1.en: 1- These enemies united together to destroy God's people, and to remove its name from among the peoples. And they made a covenant among themselves on this; that is, they are insistent on their evil, and forgot that they are defying God, before whom no one can stand.

83.2.2.en: 2- These verses are a prophecy of what happens from the demons and the wicked against the Church, but all their plots fail because God protects His Church and His children.

83.3.0.en: 6- The tabernacles of Edom, and the Ishmaelites; of Moab, and the Hagarenes; 7- Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre; 8- Assur also is joined with them: they have holpen the children of Lot. Selah. Asaph mentions a number of peoples hostile to God's people, showing their multitude, and consequently the difficulty of their wars, but because God protects His children, David was able to be victorious over all the peoples around him. And these peoples are:

83.3.1.en: 1- Edom: they are the descendants of Esau, and they dwell on the mountains of Seir which extend from the Dead Sea to the Gulf of Aqaba, and they lived in tents.

83.3.2.en: 2- The Ishmaelites: the descendants of Ishmael the son of Abraham by Hagar, and they are tribes that move in the desert between Egypt and the Persian Gulf.

83.3.3.en: 3- Moab: they are the descendants of Lot and dwelt east of the Dead Sea.

83.3.4.en: 4- The Hagarenes: tribes attributed to Hagar who live east of Gilead, which lies east of the River Jordan.

83.3.5.en: 5- Gebal: these are the mountain tribes that lived in the northern part of the mountains of Seir where the Edomites lived.

83.3.6.en: 6- The Ammonites: they too are descendants of Lot and lived east of the River Jordan and north of Moab.

83.3.7.en: 7- Amalek: tribes that lived in the regions between the north of the Arabian Peninsula and the Mediterranean Sea.

83.3.8.en: 8- The Philistines: they lived east of the Mediterranean Sea along the coast.

83.3.9.en: 9- Tyre: the greatest commercial city in the world, situated on the northeastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

83.3.10.en: 10- Assyria: a great state whose capital was Nineveh, situated on the River Tigris in northern Iraq, but it gradually weakened, and Babylon took its place, and the children of Lot, who are the two peoples Moab and the children of Ammon mentioned above, sought its help to fight God's people.

83.3.11.en: Do not be troubled by the multitude of enemies and the wars of the demons, for they are worthless before the power of God who protects you. Only hold fast to your prayers, and be steadfast in your Church and your Holy Sacraments.

83.4.s.en: (2) A request for the intervention of G

83.4.0.en: 9- Do unto them as unto the Midianites; as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook of Kison: 10- Which perished at Endor: they became as dung for the earth. 11- Make their nobles like Oreb, and like Zeeb: yea, all their princes as Zebah, and as Zalmunna: 12- Who said, Let us take to ourselves the habitations of God in possession.

83.4.1.en: Dung: the droppings and waste of beasts.

83.4.2.en: Asaph asks God to destroy the enemies of His people, as He did of old in the age of the Judges when He destroyed the Midianites by the hand of Gideon (Judg 7, 8), and as He destroyed Jabin king of Canaan and the commander of his army Sisera at the River Kishon, which lies in the north of the land of the Jews toward Galilee. And these enemies fled in the region of En-dor, which is near Megiddo, which lies south of the Sea of Galilee. And their corpses became fertilizer for the earth. And he asked also that God destroy the leaders of the enemies, as He destroyed of old the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, and likewise the kings of Midian, such as Zebah and Zalmunna. These were those who tried to occupy and possess the land of the children of Israel. In sum, he believes in God and His power able to destroy the enemies, and as He did of old He does today.

83.5.0.en: 13- O my God, make them like the jall, as the stubble before the wind. 14- As the fire burneth the rugged ground, and as the flame setteth the mountains on fire; 15- So persecute them with thy tempest, and make them afraid with thy storm.

83.5.1.en: The jall: it is straw mixed with the droppings of beasts, formed into discs and dried in the sun, and it is used for burning for heating and for lighting ovens.

83.5.2.en: Asaph asks God to put an end to the enemies, and make them nothing by His great power, like the jall, and to scatter them like stubble before the wind, and burn them with the fire of God, like the rugged ground and the mountains. And by rugged ground he means rocky places on which wild trees grow, and likewise the mountains planted with dry plants, all this burns with the flame of God. And they are also scattered by the power of God, which he likens to the tempest and the storm, so that the enemies may feel their weakness before God and His overwhelming power.

83.6.0.en: 16- Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek thy name, O LORD.

83.6.1.en: When the enemies are put to shame and are ashamed of their weakness before God, this calls them to believe in the power of God and to return to Him and leave their sins. And this shows the compassion of Asaph, or of the children of God, toward the enemies, for they seek their salvation through divine discipline; they do not hate them and want vengeance on them, but wish their return to God by faith and repentance.

83.7.0.en: 17- Let them be confounded and troubled for ever; yea, let them be put to shame, and perish: 18- That men may know that thou, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, art the most high over all the earth. But if the enemies refuse to believe in God and to turn from their sins, nothing remains for them but eternal shame and torment, and then they will know that God alone rules over all things, and they will live in their weakness and humiliation forever.

83.7.1.en: Satan wants to possess your heart and make you completely subject to him, so do not make peace with him or accept any of his evil lusts, but drive him away, by prayer, humility, and faith in God who dwells in you and is able to protect you. Dwelling in the house of the Lord. To the chief Musician upon Gittith. For the sons of Korah. A psalm. "How sweet are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!"

83.7.4.en: a- The sons of Korah, who did not die with their father Korah when the earth split open and swallowed the rebels (Num 26:11), and they served as doorkeepers of the Tabernacle of Meeting, and then the temple. And they wrote ten psalms, which are (Ps 44-Ps 48) and (Ps 84-Ps 88), and all of them are psalms that call to joy and enjoyment of fellowship with the Lord. So while divine punishment fell upon their father Korah because of his rebellion, God rewarded the sons of Korah and gave them the joy and peace which appear in these psalms that they wrote; because they did not take part in the rebellion against God.

83.7.5.en: b- David the prophet, who fled from the house of the Lord because of Saul's pursuit of him, and who longed to return to it, and was joyful on his return to worship, and even longed to build a house for the Lord.

83.7.6.en: 2- This psalm used to be said to the accompaniment of the Gittith, a musical instrument resembling the zither, which was known in the city of Gath, one of the five great Philistine cities, and the Gittith may have been a musical tune that was famous in Gath.

83.7.7.en: 3- We see in the title the word psalm, which means that these words are accompanied by a pipe.

83.7.8.en: 4- This psalm is suitable for every person who longs to worship in the house of the Lord and rejoices to be in it. It is an encouragement to the hearts of those who love God and are attached to His house.

83.7.9.en: 5- This psalm is a prophecy about the captives taken by Assyria, then Babylon, who are far from God's temple and long to return to it.

83.7.10.en: 6- This psalm gives hope to everyone whose circumstances are difficult and whose family is far from God, for in spite of the destruction of Korah, his sons were attached to the service of the house of the Lord, and wrote this psalm full of longings for the worship of God.

83.7.11.en: 7- This psalm gives longings for God's eternal dwellings, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, which is higher than all our earthly life.

83.7.12.en: 8- This psalm expresses the longings of all those who are prevented from reaching the house of God because of their particular circumstances, such as illness.

83.7.13.en: 9- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Sixth Hour in the Agpeya, in which the soul expresses its longing to dwell with God in His house, after Christ completed the redemption and reconciled the heavenly beings with the earthly, by His crucifixion at the time of the sixth hour.

84.0.s.en: (1) The sweetness of the house of G

84.0.0.en: 1- How sweet are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!

84.0.1.en: 1- The psalmist expresses his feelings toward the house of the Lord by saying how sweet; that is, he cannot describe the sweetness of the house of the Lord; because God Himself dwells in it, and so whoever comes to the house of the Lord meets God Himself, and enjoys His fellowship, and receives His blessing. He also feels his weakness before the greatness of God; therefore he describes Him as the Lord of hosts. And so a person is reverent and humble before God.

84.0.2.en: 2- He said the tabernacles of the Lord of hosts and did not say tabernacle; because in the days of David there were two tabernacles, one in Jerusalem in which was the Ark of the Covenant, and the other in Gibeon, in which were the remaining contents of the Tabernacle of Meeting. And this verse can be a prophecy about the churches of the New Testament, for they are tabernacles and not one tabernacle, as it was in the Old Testament. And it may be a prophecy about the hearts of believers in the New Testament, which become temples of the Holy Spirit, and likewise it is a prophecy about eternal life, where there are many mansions, or dwellings.

84.1.0.en: 2- My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the LORD: my heart and my flesh crieth out for the living God.

84.1.1.en: 1- The feelings of the spiritual person move toward the house of the Lord because God dwells in it, and even faint, that is, long intensely to reach the house of the Lord to enjoy seeing Him. And this means that the heart has been freed from the attachments of the world and its enticements, so that what controls the heart is the love of God. And it also means a person's faith that there is a special blessing in the house of the Lord, and a divine indwelling and grace not found outside this place, and this is our faith to this day that there is no salvation outside the Church, as St. Augustine said, and a person cannot substitute for the Church any other place such as the private chamber; for in the Church a person receives the Holy Sacraments, and knows God and is united with Him.

84.1.2.en: 2- Then the person moves with his whole being, that is, his heart and his body (his flesh) to enjoy fellowship with God. After the spiritual person believed that God is the only Being who lives forever; since the pagan gods are all dead idols, and also all the powers of the world are passing away.

84.2.0.en: 3- Yea, the sparrow hath found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, even thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God.

84.2.1.en: Swallow: a small bird with two large wings and a beautiful voice, swift in flight.

84.2.2.en: 1- The psalmist expresses his wandering in the midst of the world, and his need for settledness, and he finds no comfortable and settled place for himself except the altars of God, and by this he means the bronze altar and the altar of incense in the Tabernacle of Meeting, and then in Solomon's temple. And it is a prophecy about the churches and their altars in the New Testament, where a person enjoys partaking of the Holy Mysteries that are on the altars. And he likens himself to small birds, such as the sparrow and the swallow which search for nests or houses to settle in, and at last found a place for themselves in the house of the Lord and its courts around it; and the sparrow and the swallow are among the clean birds in the Law of Moses, and they are a symbol of the souls that dwell in and draw near to the house of the Lord, which must be pure to enjoy its blessings.

84.2.3.en: 2- The writer feels that God is his King and his God, and this shows the boldness of sonship that he has, which draws his heart to the house of the Lord. And these words are a prophecy about Christ the King and the true God of the soul that believes in Him, who gives it enjoyment in His Church of all spiritual blessings.

84.3.0.en: 4- Blessed are they that dwell in thy house: they will be ever praising thee. Selah.

84.3.1.en: 1- 1- After the psalmist has expressed the sweetness of God's house and the longing for it, he shows the great happiness that those who dwell in the house of the Lord receive, and it is noticed that in the Tabernacle of Meeting and Solomon's temple there was no dwelling of people in it, but he prophesies about the Church where believers settle in it by their attachment to the Holy Sacraments, and then by their continued steadfastness in the Church in its prayers and praises they become worthy of the eternal dwelling in the Kingdom of Heaven, where they praise God forever, sharing with the heavenly beings in the praise of God.

84.3.2.en: 2- These verses end with the word Selah, which is a musical pause for meditating on the sweetness of the house of the Lord, being satisfied by fellowship with God, and praising His holy name

84.3.3.en: Hasten to the Church to meet God in His house. He is waiting for you to embrace you and satisfy you, so that your heart rejoices, and your prayers and praises increase.

84.4.s.en: (2) The blessings of the house of the Lord

84.4.0.en: 5- Blessed are the people whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of thy house.

84.4.1.en: 1- The psalm shows the happiness of those who believe in God, and calls them blessed because their strength is God, and that is by keeping His commandments in their hearts and lives, for these are the ways of the house of the Lord in their hearts, so that the feelings of their hearts lift them above earthly things, attached to God, so they long not only for the house of the Lord that is on earth, but also for the heavenly house which is the Kingdom of Heaven.

84.4.2.en: 2- The psalm calls blessed the believers who boast in God; because they loved Him more than everything in the world, so that material things and honor have become passing in their eyes, and nothing greater than God remains for them to boast in, and they remain in their love for God by keeping His commandments, these are the ways of God's house that are in their hearts, and by this they love everyone around them too.

84.5.0.en: 6- Passing through the valley of weeping, they make it a spring; yea, with blessings they cover Moreh.

84.5.1.en: Moreh: the early rain that falls in the autumn. It is necessary for watering the crop at the beginning of its life.

84.5.2.en: 1- The psalm shows the means by which believers receive God's blessings. It declares that this takes place through their passing through the valley of weeping, which is one of the roads leading to Jerusalem, and it was very dry; so that whoever walked in it was exposed to death by thirst. Therefore they used to dig pits around it which filled with rain water; to help the one walking on the road to drink from them. That is, whoever passes on the road to Jerusalem to worship and bow down to God bears sufferings and prays and his tears flow, but if he perseveres on the road his heart becomes a spring of water full of blessings; because God pours out upon him many graces as the early rains pour upon the crop, so whoever strives and bears sufferings the Holy Spirit pours out upon him many blessings, like the rains of Moreh, and even more, so blessings are given him from every side.

84.5.3.en: 2- The valley of weeping is the tears of repentance that become like a spring of water welling up from the heart of the penitent, turning the dryness of his heart into abundant waters, and his life is filled with divine blessings. So here he calls the penitent blessed and promises them all God's blessings.

84.6.0.en: 7- They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God.

84.6.1.en: 1- Then the psalm declares a new blessing for the striving believers, that they advance from strength to strength, that is, they are not only strong, but their strength increases gradually through their spiritual striving and their victories, so they receive more and more grace, and likewise acquire virtue after virtue. And more than this, when they show their faithfulness in spiritual striving on earth, and receive divine strength supporting them, they are lifted up after this to heaven; to receive great strength, so they are propelled into a strong relationship with God that makes their souls rejoice forever.

84.6.2.en: 2- And after this a new blessing that believers receive, which is that they are seen before God in Zion, and he means Jerusalem where the house of the Lord is, so they enjoy not only the worship of God, but God sees them, and he did not say that they see God; for their seeing God gives them enjoyment of the sweetness of His fellowship, but God's seeing them gives them care, love, and inexpressible joy, which is a pledge of what they receive in the Kingdom of Heaven.

84.6.3.en: The heavenly Kingdom is available to you here on earth if you draw near to God in His house to behold His glory through His Holy Sacraments. And when you lift up prayers before Him, His mercies and blessings pour out upon you. Take care lest the devil hinder you from being constantly in His Church.

84.7.0.en: 8- O LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer: give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.

84.7.1.en: 1- After the believer has received blessings in the house of the Lord, he asks Him to hear his prayer. And he gives God the title Lord of hosts, that is, the mighty One, able to do all things, and consequently He can answer all his requests. Then he advances to a higher degree, and asks that God give ear to him. And he gives Him here the title God of Jacob; because He is the God who appeared of old to Jacob on the ladder reaching up to heaven. So the believer rises above his material and spiritual requests to ask to see God Himself, as Jacob saw Him. And God is the same yesterday, today and forever, so He is not only with Jacob, but with all his descendants who walk with God as he did. And by this the psalm lifts us from material worship such as sacrifices to spiritual worship that requires seeing God, and enjoying being in His presence.

84.7.2.en: 2- This verse ends with the word Selah, which is a musical extension for a person to meditate on the sweetness of seeing God.

84.8.0.en: 9- Behold, O God our buckler, and look upon the face of thine Anointed.

84.8.1.en: Our buckler: the buckler is the large shield. And the shield is a wooden piece with a loop at the back in which the soldier puts his hand, and he moves this wooden piece before his face and his body to protect him from the arrows of the enemy. So it is a defensive instrument of war to protect the soldier.

84.8.2.en: 1- Believers look to God as their protection, for He is not only a shield for them but a buckler, that is, a large shield, representing complete protection. So they call on God and give Him the title "our buckler" and ask Him to look upon them; because they are confident of His love, so when He looks upon them, He stretches out His hand and protects them from all enemies. And this shows that they feel wars surrounding them, and need God to protect them.

84.8.3.en: 2- If the writer of the psalm is David, he asks God to look upon him; because he is the anointed king over his people, and he asks merely for God's turning to him, for this gives him all the protection he needs. And this verse is also a prophecy about Christ who speaks to the Father as in His intercessory prayer (Jn 17), and asks for the turning toward Him during the sufferings He endured at His arrest and crucifixion; to declare that they were real sufferings. And it is also a prophecy about the believers in the New Testament who ask God to turn to Christ who dwells in them, as they are anointed with the Myron for the indwelling of the Holy Spirit in them, and they are members of the Body of Christ who is the Head and the face. And they intercede through Christ in all their petitions; because without Christ they have no acceptance before the Father.

84.9.0.en: 10- For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I have chosen to stand at the threshold in the house of my God rather than dwell in the tents of the wicked.

84.9.1.en: 1- The psalm declares that spending one day in the house of the Lord, that is, in prayer, worship, and enjoyment of fellowship with God, is better than a thousand days that a person spends in the midst of the passing pleasures of the world far from God. And the one day is the day of the Resurrection, which surpasses the thousands of days in the Old Testament in which humanity awaited the salvation of God. And the one day is the last day of the Lord, in which the believers enter into the glories of eternal life, which is better than a thousand days in earthly life. And the one day is eternity itself; because eternity is day without night, so it is one day better than a thousand days on earth.

84.9.2.en: 2- The psalm also declares that standing at the threshold of the house of the Lord is better than sitting and settling in the tents of the wicked, and by this he means the places of the world with all its lusts. Because standing at the door of the house of the Lord gives a person enjoyment of God's blessing and the sense of His presence. And perhaps the sons of Korah, who were charged with guarding the doors of the house of the Lord, felt the greatness of their position and its blessing; because they stand always before God, and this is better than any other place in the world, indeed this is true settledness; because being in the presence of God is life and being far from Him is death.

84.10.0.en: 11- For the LORD God is a sun and buckler: the LORD will give mercy and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.

84.10.1.en: 1- The psalm describes God as a sun, that is, He is the One who shines upon His children, and upon the whole world, to give them an illumined way that brings them to Him. For He guides everyone who desires to live with Him, for He is the Sun of righteousness. And He is also the buckler, that is, the Protector of His children from all the wars of the devil.

84.10.2.en: 2- And God gives mercy to His children by forgiving their sins and accepting their repentance, and also grants them the glory of life with Him, so they are adorned with virtue. And this glory that they enjoy on earth is a pledge of the eternal glory that cannot be expressed. And God by nature is good, that is, the source of all good in the world; therefore He does not withhold good from His children, but pours it out upon them, to satisfy them and draw them to His Kingdom.

84.11.0.en: 12- O LORD of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee. The psalm ends with the blessing of the person who trusts in God, that is, the one who repents of his sins; so that he received God's mercies and forgiveness, and then enjoyed His glories, and the highest glory is seeing God, and enjoying His fellowship. And God, the Lord of hosts, is strong and able to keep those who trust in Him in constant enjoyment of Him on earth as long as they hold fast to Him, and then forever in His heavenly Kingdom.

84.11.1.en: I wish you would give priority to going to church over all your ties in the world. Then you will enjoy the sense of God's presence, and receive blessings without end.

84.11.2.en: The mercies of God. To the chief Musician. For the sons of Korah. A psalm. "LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land) "... v. 1) Introduction:

84.11.3.en: 1- Its writer: the sons of Korah, who did not take part in the rebellion of their father Korah against the priesthood, so they lived and God blessed them.

84.11.4.en: 2- When was it written? It was written after the first return from the captivity, and before the completion of the return of the following groups of returnees.

84.11.5.en: 3- This psalm recalls God's former mercies to His people, and asks the completion of His mercies in the present for the return from the captivity, and the completion of the building of the temple and Jerusalem and its walls. And it hopes for the continuance of God's mercies in the future.

84.11.6.en: 4- This psalm is a prophecy about the liberation from the captivity and bondage of the devil by Christ the Redeemer; and therefore it is considered one of the Messianic psalms.

84.11.7.en: 5- This psalm is suitable for the soul that has begun repentance and received God's forgiveness, so it asks His help to complete its repentance and live a new life with God.

84.11.8.en: 6- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Sixth Hour in which we remember the crucifixion of Christ and His cry that frees us from the captivity of Satan and binds him.
